solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Endless last-minute stirring for pick-me-up (9)

indicatorNotes.Endless: a word with no end loses its final letter, here the E of minute
indicatorNotes.stirring: stirring moves things round, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: LAST-MINUTE with its end E dropped

annotation.surface: A last-minute rush that stirs someone up like a pick-me-up.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen in last-minute is ignored; the nine letters left after trimming the E rearrange exactly.
annotation.definitionFit: Coffee, tonic or a drug that perks you up all count as a stimulant; pick-me-up is the informal synonym.

entries.clue: Street with spot for taxis (5)

annotation.surface: A street with a place where cabs wait.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a joining word but supplies letters of its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A taxi stand, or cab rank, is the kerbside place where cabs queue waiting for fares.

entries.clue: What can be used to cut stone under River Test (10,7)

annotation.definition: What can be used to cut

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, one thing under another is written below it, so the stone comes last

blocks.note: the Indus, a river of Pakistan

annotation.surface: Something to cut stone with, found beneath the River Test in Hampshire.
annotation.walkthrough: The River Test is a real English river, famous for trout, so 'cut stone under River Test' reads as a place; the capital R and T make it look like one name when it is two separate words.
annotation.definitionFit: Industrial diamonds are hard, low-grade stones set into saws and drill bits for cutting.

entries.clue: Mysterious mushrooms springing up in one (11)

indicatorNotes.springing up: springing up rises from the ground, so in a down clue the word reads upwards
indicatorNotes.in: the mushrooms are placed in the word for one, splitting it

annotation.surface: Mysterious mushrooms popping up in a single clump.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' usually gives I or A; here it is the adjective, as in 'the country is now one'.
annotation.definitionFit: Something unspecified is left unstated or unnamed, which is a loose sense of mysterious.

entries.clue: Air-conditioning with a bit of American intensity (6)

blocks.note: a small American coin, a bit of American money

annotation.surface: An air-conditioner blasting with American force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A bit of American' looks like a letter pick from the word; it is a coin.
annotation.definitionFit: Accent means stress or emphasis, the extra force put on a syllable or note.

entries.clue: Moderated rage pursued by editor (8)

indicatorNotes.pursued by: something pursued has its chaser behind it, so the editor follows the rage

annotation.surface: A calmed-down fury with an editor on its tail.
annotation.walkthrough: The irony is in the surface: rage is exactly what a tempered reaction lacks.
annotation.definitionFit: To temper criticism is to soften it, tone it down, so tempered and moderated are synonyms.

entries.clue: State Post Office? It’s confused (5)

indicatorNotes.confused: confused letters are muddled up, so ITS changes its order

annotation.surface: A customer baffled by the state-run Post Office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation beside the Post Office; it is the verb, to put forward.
annotation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward an idea as a premise for argument, the formal sense of state.

entries.clue: Smear managers for item sold by builders’ merchant (12)

annotation.surface: Someone badmouthing the bosses of a building-supplies firm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smear managers' reads as defamation; it is two plain synonyms end to end.
annotation.definitionFit: Builders' merchants are British trade suppliers of building materials, and gypsum wallboard sheets are a staple of their stock.

entries.clue: British unknown joining two teams adjoining each other (4,2,4)

indicatorNotes.joining: the British unknown acts as the joint between the two teams, sitting in the middle

blocks.note: x, y and z are algebra's unknowns

annotation.surface: An anonymous British player linking up two teams.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer describes its own construction: two teams sit next to each other with the British unknown between.
annotation.definitionFit: Things placed next to one another, touching or in a row, are adjoining each other.

entries.clue: Refresher working in very little time, not needing all of it (5)

indicatorNotes.in: working is placed in the shortened time word
indicatorNotes.not needing all of it: the time word is used without all its letters, losing the last one

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: A pick-me-up that works quickly without taking up much time.
annotation.walkthrough: The very little time is the British 'just a tick', meaning a moment.
annotation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative drink or medicine that invigorates, much as a refresher does.

entries.clue: Flowing westwards, a river also falls? (7)

indicatorNotes.Flowing westwards: in an across clue, west is leftwards, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A westward-flowing river that also has a waterfall.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'falls' is the definition, not a verb, and the waterfall named is on a river too.
annotation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls is the famous waterfall on the border between New York state and Ontario.

entries.clue: Theatre to copy style when mounting writer’s material (9)

indicatorNotes.mounting: mounting means climbing, so in a down clue the pieces read upwards

annotation.surface: A theatre company imitating a playwright's manner.
annotation.walkthrough: TON for style is an old borrowing from French, as in 'the ton' of Regency high society.
annotation.definitionFit: Notepaper is the stationery a letter-writer uses, the material a writer puts pen to.

entries.clue: Antony Cecil being treated for circulation (11)

indicatorNotes.being treated: something treated is processed and altered, so the names' letters are reworked

annotation.surface: A patient named Antony Cecil getting medical care for poor blood flow.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'circulation' blood; it is air turning round a high-pressure system.
annotation.definitionFit: An anticyclone is a weather system of winds rotating around a centre of high pressure, a circulation of air.

entries.clue: What’s wrapped round in filo? I add flavoured mayo (5)

indicatorNotes.wrapped: the answer is wrapped up inside the run of letters that follows
indicatorNotes.round: turned round, the concealed letters read from right to left

blocks.note: surface padding that frames the question

annotation.surface: A cook asking what goes inside filo pastry and offering garlic mayo.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark hides the join: the answer runs across 'filo? I add' and backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provençal sauce of mayonnaise flavoured with garlic.

entries.clue: Retaliate for special constable killed in search (6)

indicatorNotes.killed in: the constable is killed off, removed from inside the search word

blocks.note: to scavenge = to search for scraps

annotation.surface: Revenge sought for a police officer killed during a search.
annotation.walkthrough: A special constable is a volunteer British police officer, abbreviated SC; the surface sets up a revenge plot to match.
annotation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to punish whoever did it in return, which is retaliating for it.

entries.clue: Mountains, Scottish ones either side of Dee (5)

indicatorNotes.either side of: the Scottish ones split and stand on both sides of the letter

blocks.note: the letter D spelt as a word

annotation.surface: Scottish mountains flanking the River Dee.
annotation.walkthrough: The Dee is a Scottish river, so the surface points to Scotland; the mountains are in South America.
annotation.definitionFit: The Andes is the great mountain range running down western South America.

entries.clue: Crew chasing miles to fill fish order (7)

indicatorNotes.chasing: a chaser runs behind, so the crew word comes after the miles
indicatorNotes.to fill: the pair is stuffed inside the fish like a filling

blocks.note: to man a ship = to crew it

annotation.surface: A fishing crew racing for miles to fill a fish order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fish order' reads as a restaurant order; the fish is the container and the order is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A command is an instruction that must be obeyed, the same as an order.

entries.clue: Out and barking at the moon (3,2,4)

blocks.note: away from your house, as when a caller finds nobody in
crazy, as in 'the lights are on but nobody's in'

annotation.surface: A dog let out to howl at the moon.
annotation.walkthrough: Barking here is British slang for mad, and someone mad is said to have nobody in upstairs.
annotation.definitionFit: Out means absent from your house; the second reading is a jokey version of 'not all there', meaning mad.

entries.clue: Bond outside Royal Navy is after underworld intelligence? (11)

indicatorNotes.outside: the bond word goes outside the navy, enclosing it
indicatorNotes.is after: the enclosed unit is placed after the underworld, coming second

blocks.note: Dis, the Roman god and realm of the underworld

annotation.surface: James Bond, outside the Navy, gathering underworld intelligence.
annotation.walkthrough: Bond the spy and 'intelligence' make a secret-service picture; the question mark admits that intelligence here is good judgement, not spying.
annotation.definitionFit: Discernment is keen judgement and insight, one sense of intelligence as mental sharpness.

entries.clue: Support getting ready for holiday hiking (11)

annotation.surface: Help packing for a walking holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about the answer itself; nothing is misdirected except where the first word ends.
annotation.definitionFit: Backpacking is travelling on foot with your gear carried in a rucksack, a form of hiking.

entries.clue: Disease besetting rook and crow? (6)

indicatorNotes.besetting: to beset is to surround and attack, so the disease wraps round the rook

blocks.note: surface link joining rook to crow

annotation.surface: A disease afflicting rooks and crows.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes rook a bird, and so it is; in the wordplay rook is only the chess letter. The question mark marks crow as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Corvids are the crow family of birds, which also includes rooks, ravens, jays and magpies.

entries.clue: Mix and invent shade (10)

blocks.note: to cross breeds = to mix them
to hatch a plan = to invent it

annotation.surface: Mixing paint to create a new colour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shade' looks like a colour noun; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To crosshatch is to darken a drawing with sets of crossing parallel lines, an artist's shading technique.

entries.clue: Northeast supporter pens petition for area surrounding Lincoln (8)

indicatorNotes.pens: to pen is to shut in, as animals in a pen, so the supporter encloses the petition

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting garment

annotation.surface: A northeastern backer drafting a petition for the land around Lincoln in England.
annotation.walkthrough: Lincoln suggests the English cathedral city; it is the capital of a US state.
annotation.definitionFit: Lincoln is Nebraska's state capital, so the whole state is an area that surrounds it.

entries.clue: Having a whiff of a habitual response around travellers (8)

indicatorNotes.around: the habitual response is split and placed around the travellers

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

annotation.surface: Someone wrinkling their nose by habit at the smell of passing travellers.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain 'travellers' is the usual word for itinerant communities, which is why the setter can use it for the Roma.
annotation.definitionFit: Aromatic describes something giving off a noticeable smell or fragrance, which is having a whiff.

entries.clue: Still fast, keeping in condition (6)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so the fast word holds the condition inside

annotation.surface: Still quick, staying in good shape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' and 'fast' look like adjectives that could both define the answer; still is the verb, to calm.
annotation.definitionFit: To pacify an angry crowd or a crying baby is to calm or quieten it, the verb still.

entries.clue: National celebration Bolivia at first arranged in Slough (8,2,7)

indicatorNotes.arranged: arranged means set in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters are placed inside the bog word

blocks.note: a slough is a bog, a fen; the anagram goes in between its E and N

annotation.surface: A South American national holiday being staged in the English town of Slough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like a first-letter instruction on Bolivia, but it is plain fodder. Slough is a Berkshire town, and a slough is also a bog.
annotation.definitionFit: The Festival of Britain was a 1951 national exhibition held across the UK to lift postwar spirits.

entries.clue: Duck! Vehicle’s lost what looks like wheel (6)

indicatorNotes.lost: the vehicle has lost a wheel-shaped letter, which is removed

blocks.note: the letter O is wheel-shaped, removed

annotation.surface: A shout to take cover as a vehicle loses a wheel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck!' reads as a warning to dodge; it is the bird.
annotation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark-plumaged sea duck of northern coasts.

entries.clue: Tax beasts of burden dispatched carrying mass (10)

indicatorNotes.carrying: to carry is to hold, so the dispatched word holds the mass inside

annotation.surface: A levy on pack animals sent off with a heavy load.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tax' reads as a verb about burdening; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: An assessment is an amount levied by an authority, such as a local rate or duty, so a tax.

entries.clue: Uniform belonging to a knight? (2,1,5)

blocks.note: consistent, all of the same kind
a knight is a chess man, so what belongs to it belongs to one of the chessmen

annotation.surface: A uniform owned by a knight in armour.
annotation.walkthrough: Uniform looks like clothing to go with the knight; it is the adjective, and the chess knight is the other reading.
annotation.definitionFit: Things that match throughout are said to be of a piece, meaning uniform; a knight is a chess piece.

entries.clue: Stop sorry household cooking (4,4,6)

indicatorNotes.cooking: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are cooked into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A plea to stop the dreadful cooking in a sorry home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop' works as a whole command, spoken to someone rushing ahead.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to wait and not rush, an exclamation meaning stop.

entries.clue: Even decided to enter old field (8)

indicatorNotes.to enter: entering means going inside, so the decided word goes into the old field

blocks.note: mead is a poetic old word for meadow

annotation.surface: Someone finally resolving to step into an old field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb opening the sentence; it is the adjective, steady.
annotation.definitionFit: A measured pace or tone is steady and regular, which is one sense of even.

entries.clue: Sidney and Edward casually associated (5)

indicatorNotes.casually: casual speech uses nicknames, so both names are cut to their short forms

blocks.note: Sidney shortened to its first three letters, the nickname
Edward cut short to its nickname

annotation.surface: Two men who happen to be acquaintances.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Casually' works on both names, and also misleads as a description of the acquaintance.
annotation.definitionFit: Having sided with someone is to have taken their part, so to have associated yourself with them.

entries.clue: This fellow involved in Conservative speculation (6)

indicatorNotes.involved in: someone involved in a group is inside it, so this fellow goes into the party

blocks.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

annotation.surface: A man caught up in Conservative Party gossip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speculation' suggests rumour or investment; here it is a supposition.
annotation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition not yet proven, as in 'in theory', which is speculation.

entries.clue: Disputant breaking tiny child’s flower (10)

indicatorNotes.breaking: the disputant breaks into the child, splitting that word open

blocks.note: a mite is a small child

annotation.surface: A squabbling kid breaking a toddler's flower.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in 'child's' is just part of the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A marguerite is the ox-eye daisy, a white-petalled garden flower.

entries.clue: Puff during good sprint is something annoying (6)

indicatorNotes.during: one thing during another falls in its middle, so the puff sits inside

blocks.note: a puff is a promotional plug, an ad

annotation.surface: Getting out of breath in the middle of a sprint is a nuisance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Puff' reads as breath; it is publicity.
annotation.definitionFit: A gadfly is a biting horsefly, and figuratively a person who provokes and irritates others.

entries.clue: Auden memoirs recollected bad behaviour (12)

indicatorNotes.recollected: read as re-collected, the letters are gathered up again in a different order

annotation.surface: W H Auden recalling his misdeeds in his memoirs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, fitting memoirs; split as re-collected, it gathers the letters anew.
annotation.definitionFit: A misdemeanour is a minor wrongdoing or offence, a piece of bad behaviour.

entries.clue: Unprofessional partner invested in gold from Eire losing capital (10)

indicatorNotes.invested in: money invested in something is put into it, so the partner goes inside the gold
indicatorNotes.losing capital: capital here is the capital letter, so the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter, I, is dropped

annotation.surface: A shady partner putting money into Irish gold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money to go with invested and gold, or as Dublin; it is the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Amateurish means clumsy and lacking skill, the opposite of polished professional work.

entries.clue: Just, say, came down on heretic (11)

blocks.note: a follower of Arius, the 4th-century heretic

annotation.surface: An authority simply cracking down on a heretic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just, say' reads like 'only, say'; Just is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: An egalitarian system treats everyone as equal, which is a fair and just one.

entries.clue: Showed sadness for parking I restricted (6)

annotation.surface: A driver feeling sorry for themselves over restricted parking.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'for' belongs to the definition, which needs it to match the transitive verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To have pitied someone is to have felt sorrow and compassion at their misfortune.

entries.clue: Island’s accepting European funds (5)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept is to take in, so the island word takes the European inside

annotation.surface: An island taking EU money.
annotation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, the usual 'Island' of crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Your means are the money and resources you have to live on, your funds.

entries.clue: How to make Logan manage more or less satisfactorily (6,5)

blocks.note: the answer read as an instruction: jumble the letters of its second word and you make LOGAN
a straight definition of the answer

annotation.surface: Instructions for somehow getting by.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is itself the wordplay, a scramble signal followed by the letters it turns into the name.
annotation.definitionFit: To muddle along is to get by without much plan or skill, coping more or less adequately.

entries.clue: Tense model following a lot of publicity (10)

indicatorNotes.following: the model comes after the publicity, following it in the answer
indicatorNotes.a lot of: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: PLUG (a bit of publicity) minus its last letter
a model pupil is a perfect one

annotation.surface: A model tense after a whirl of media attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous, suiting a model; it is the grammar term.
annotation.definitionFit: The pluperfect, or past perfect, is the verb tense of 'had done', for an action before another past one.

entries.clue: Work by Bach Hallé reproduced mostly badly? (7,7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.badly: something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A Bach piece played poorly by the Hallé orchestra.
annotation.walkthrough: The Hallé is a Manchester orchestra, so reproduced looks like performed; the accent on é is ignored.
annotation.definitionFit: Bach wrote dozens of chorale preludes, short organ pieces built on Lutheran hymn tunes.

entries.clue: Disaffected nuisance crashed, neglecting power and pressure (9)

indicatorNotes.neglecting: to neglect is to leave out, so both words drop the letter for power and pressure

blocks.note: to prang is British slang for to crash a car
P for power and P for pressure, both removed

annotation.surface: A troublemaker who crashed, disregarding power and pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: Each P comes off the front of its word, one for power and one for pressure.
annotation.definitionFit: Estranged means alienated from people you were once close to, which is disaffected.

entries.clue: Joyous months over in woodland space (8)

indicatorNotes.over: turned over, the months abbreviation reads from right to left
indicatorNotes.in: the turned months are placed in the woodland space

annotation.surface: Happy months passed in a forest clearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as time passing; it turns the months round.
annotation.definitionFit: Gladsome is an old literary word for cheerful and delightful, meaning joyous.

entries.clue: Curse article found in hat — not the topper (8)

indicatorNotes.found in: the article is found inside the headless hat
indicatorNotes.not the topper: in a down clue the topper is the top letter, so the hat loses its first letter

annotation.surface: A spell hidden in a hat, but not a top hat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topper' looks like a top hat; it is the top letter of a Panama.
annotation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal church curse of excommunication, hence any curse.

entries.clue: Commercial division lacking direction (6)

annotation.surface: A company department that has lost its way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' reads as an adjective with 'division'; it is the TV ad.
annotation.definitionFit: A boat adrift floats with no one steering; a person adrift is aimless, without purpose.

entries.clue: Drug’s taken about a minute for chemical to affect brain (8)

indicatorNotes.taken about: the drug is taken round the rest, placed about it on both sides

annotation.surface: A drug taken for about a minute to alter the mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as roughly a minute; it tells the drug to go round.
annotation.definitionFit: Dopamine is a neurotransmitter, a chemical messenger that acts on the brain's reward system.

entries.clue: Everything except headless fish’s left for one (3,3)

indicatorNotes.headless: a headless word has lost its first letter, so the fish drops its H
indicatorNotes.for: for means in place of, so the left letter stands in for one

blocks.note: the Roman numeral, which L replaces

annotation.surface: A fish with its head cut off and the rest thrown away.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is taken literally here; in speech the phrase more usually means almost.
annotation.definitionFit: All but X covers every item except X, which is why the phrase also means very nearly.

entries.clue: Which people, keeping nothing quiet, go quickly? (6)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so the people and quiet hold the nothing between them

annotation.surface: A question about which people, while being quiet, can move fast.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark hides that the answer is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To whoosh is to rush past at speed with a sweeping sound, so to go quickly.

entries.clue: Beginner’s book of paint (6)

blocks.note: the first coat applied to bare wood or metal

annotation.surface: A starter guide to painting.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses share a root: the first stage, of learning or of painting.
annotation.definitionFit: The word means both an elementary reading book and an undercoat that prepares a surface.

entries.clue: Cast had garbled English play (5,6)

indicatorNotes.Cast: to cast is to throw, like dice, so the letters land in a new order

annotation.surface: Actors who mangled the English of a play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as the actors and 'garbled' as the anagram signal; in fact garbled is fodder and Cast does the mixing.
annotation.definitionFit: Hedda Gabler is Henrik Ibsen's 1891 drama about a trapped, destructive woman.

entries.clue: What archaeologist is casually said to do to discoveries in fact? (5)

indicatorNotes.casually said: in relaxed speech 'date them' is slurred, which is how the answer sounds

blocks.clueFragment: What archaeologist is casually said to do to discoveries

annotation.surface: A question about what archaeologists actually do with their finds.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the last word is the definition; everything before describes the sound.
annotation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, the singular of data, so a fact.

entries.clue: Sensational hat getting regularly furry inside (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter of furry is taken
indicatorNotes.inside: the chosen letters go inside the hat word

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat
surface link: the hat gets a lining

annotation.surface: An outrageous hat with a fur lining.
annotation.walkthrough: The alternate letters are the second and fourth of furry.
annotation.definitionFit: Lurid means shockingly vivid or gruesome, as in lurid headlines, so sensational.

entries.clue: Unusual to convert local (11)

annotation.surface: It is rare for a local to change their religion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Convert' and 'local' look like nouns, a religious convert and a pub; each is read another way.
annotation.definitionFit: Alternative in the sense of unconventional, outside the mainstream: alternative comedy, alternative medicine.

entries.clue: Drunk in the middle of week for choice (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the drunk word is placed in the letters taken from week
indicatorNotes.the middle of: the middle of a word is its central letters, here the two Es

annotation.surface: Getting drunk midweek as a lifestyle choice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Choice' is the adjective: select, top quality.
annotation.definitionFit: Elite means the best of a group, select and top quality, which is the adjective choice.

entries.clue: Boat race team shortly set off in rowing boat (9)

indicatorNotes.shortly: said shortly, the name is cut to its abbreviation

blocks.note: Oxford University, one of the Boat Race crews, abbreviated

annotation.surface: The Boat Race crew setting off shortly in their boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames.
annotation.definitionFit: An outrigger is a racing skiff whose rowlocks sit on brackets projecting beyond the hull.

entries.clue: Part of embryo from red oxen shows this returning (7)

indicatorNotes.shows: the words show the answer openly, concealed in their letters
indicatorNotes.returning: returning means going back, so the concealed letters read from right to left

blocks.note: stands for the answer being shown

annotation.surface: Embryo tissue taken from red cattle being sent back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This' points back at the definition, the thing the letters show.
annotation.definitionFit: The exoderm, or ectoderm, is the outermost germ layer of an early embryo.

entries.clue: Briefly feverish, going after love from a Gulf state (5)

indicatorNotes.Briefly: said briefly, the word is cut short and loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.going after: the shortened word goes after the love, following it

annotation.surface: A brief fever of love for someone from the Gulf.
annotation.walkthrough: Oman is on the Arabian Peninsula, at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.
annotation.definitionFit: Omani is the adjective for things and people of Oman, a sultanate on the Gulf.

entries.clue: Note backing covering skirt for man? (7)

indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards, the note is read from right to left
indicatorNotes.covering: the reversed note wraps round the skirt like a cover

blocks.note: doh, the first note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A man in a kilt? A skirt for a man.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark says man is an example: humans are one kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Hominids are the family of great apes that includes humans, so man is one example.

entries.clue: Discourage chap avoiding soap (5)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: something avoided is kept away, so the chap is left out of the soap word

annotation.surface: A man put off from washing.
annotation.walkthrough: The deleted chap is at the end of the soap, so the front survives.
annotation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to put them off doing something, usually by fear of consequences.

entries.clue: Pride of Aragorn bothered Celeborn and Elrond initially (9)

indicatorNotes.bothered: bothered means agitated and troubled, so the letters are stirred up
indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the first letters of the elves are used

blocks.note: first letters of Celeborn and Elrond

annotation.surface: Tolkien's proud Aragorn irritating the elves Celeborn and Elrond.
annotation.walkthrough: All three are Lord of the Rings characters; the names are pure letter supply.
annotation.definitionFit: Arrogance is an overbearing sense of your own importance, a haughty form of pride.
